title: Seven Clubs, only one honor
author_notes: EC-055 checkpoint-3 coverage: a third bid_sizing scenario, deliberately different in shape from bid_training_012 (short, near-solid six-card run) and bid_training_013 (moderate five-card suit plus two side Aces). Here the trump suit is long (seven cards) but carries only one honor, the Ace; the sizing question is how much credit exceptional length alone supports without top-card concentration, contrasted against bid_training_012's opposite profile (short but near-solid). Single trump offered (Clubs), so the decision is purely trick-count judgment. Independent hand; ratings are authored judgments, not probabilities or guaranteed outcomes.

feedback.title: Safe, but undersells the length
feedback.summary: Four is secure from the Ace of Clubs alone, without needing any of the six low Clubs to ever be established.
points: Control: the Ace of Clubs is one certain trick, checkable directly against the hand shown.
This target does not need the suit's exceptional length to produce anything further.
A stronger target is defensible from this same length; four is not wrong, just conservative.

feedback.title: The Ace plus exceptional length
feedback.summary: Five combines the one certain trick with the seven-card suit's length, a different kind of support than a suit headed by several honors.
points: Control: the Ace of Clubs is a certain trick.
Probable, not certain: seven cards is unusually long; once opponents' Clubs are exhausted, a low Club left in hand can become a winner by length alone.
This does not require every remaining Club to run clean, only that the suit's length contributes past the Ace.

feedback.title: Needs several rounds to run clean
feedback.summary: Six asks the suit's length to produce two extra tricks beyond the Ace, not just one.
points: A single honor does not, by itself, establish two further length tricks.
The King of Hearts and Queen-less side suits offer nothing to fall back on if the Clubs do not run as cleanly as hoped.
This is not an unreasonable attempt, but it depends on more rounds going well than a five-trick target does.
